Establishes the live derivation reads the host profile object and distinguishes values. Does NOT establish that execute refuses.

Only line :260 (`host_profile_digest=profile_digest(self._f5_host)`) differs. The original UNREACHABLE-ISOLATED record used the pin-export fixture (F4-only + policy_binding) where held == host; that record is not contradicted for that fixture, but it does not hold as a general statement - NEW FINDING (reported, not a correction).

### 2.2 scope.authority_domain (A25(a))
- C (Q2-A1): two genuine worlds (d1 customer-refunds, d2 other-domain; manifest, proposal, resolver, Registry selection all self-consistent). Each minted member's scope.authority_domain equals the domain in that world's own manifest authority_context; full member diff == {digest, members.scope.authority_domain}; digests recompute; the base-binding diff between the two worlds is exactly {manifest_digest, proposal_commitment}, which demonstrates the dependency chain below. Does NOT establish refusal.
- P: A19 execute row [scope.authority_domain] (reseal) reused by citation; the original M06 SURVIVED record (constant live value) is permanent predecessor evidence and is the reason persisted-only edits cannot establish live-side sensitivity.
- R / structural: the member value is authority[1] read from the host manifest (registry_governed_lifecycle.py:81 _declared_authority, :199 _gl_common_members, effective_configuration_binding.py:130 scope_identity). The manifest digest is a base-binding member that must equal commitment(self.manifest) (bounded.py:2619) and the resolver domain must equal the manifest domain (bounded.py:2298). Natural live-side routes therefore always move manifest_digest and proposal_commitment as well. Observed guard order (Q2-A2): (iii) original A25(a) route -> [authority_domain_mismatch, manifest_digest_mismatch]; (i) consistent d2 world with the un-rebuilt proposal P1 -> [approval_operation_binding_mismatch, manifest_digest_mismatch]; in both the ECB is never consulted (lifecycle.py:267 returns base reasons unchanged). (ii) consistent d2 world, rebuilt P2 against D1 -> reaches the ECB comparison and refuses with [authorization_binding_changed], but the diff is base {manifest_digest, proposal_commitment} plus ECB {digest, domain}: JOINT. Natural isolation is structurally impossible on the live side without disabling a guard; none was disabled.
- E (Q2-A3, GRAFT): see section 4 for the construction and its validity argument. Result: single [authorization_binding_changed], base diff [], ECB diff exactly {digest, members.scope.authority_domain}, classifier "mismatch"; the byte-untouched d2 copy and a neutral graft (member of an identical-domain independent world) both acknowledged with one destination call.
- Does NOT establish: natural reachability (there is none in the supported operating model; the graft needs the documented unsigned-store writer capability, the same capability class as the documented rollback/forge limit); it does not establish anything about who could perform such a write.
- Kill evidence: D06-M06 (constant domain) makes the graft EXECUTE (acknowledged, 1 destination call), Q2-A1 fail 4 checks, Q2-A2 fail its ECB-content check only. This is a live-side kill by an end-to-end case; the original run's M06 SURVIVED record stands unchanged as predecessor evidence.

### 2.3 effective_profile_digest (A25(e))
- C (Q3-H2): equals the own commitment of the held effective profile and equals the persisted catalogue_digest (runtime_authority.py:475); differs from host digest on the F5 fixture. By construction it is redundant with catalogue_digest in the same persisted dict.
- P: A19 execute row [effective_profile_digest] (reseal) reused by citation, not rerun.
- R: any natural live change to the effective profile moves catalogue_digest and approval_commitment; without a re-issued approval the approval guard fires first (Q3-E1: only [runtime_authority_approval_mismatch], ECB code absent). With a re-issued approval (a supported host duty) the ECB comparison is reached (Q3-E2: [authorization_binding_changed]) but the live-vs-persisted diff is base {approval_commitment, catalogue_digest} plus ECB {digest, effective_profile_digest, families.0.effective_policy_digest}: JOINT.
- E: guard-first (E1) and joint (E2) only. No isolated end-to-end claim is made or available. Not attempted (heavy and still joint): the freshness-extension construction; a graft with a donor of a different effective profile (would also move the base binding). Not killable end-to-end by natural routes: a mutant dropping this member is outcome-equivalent there (catalogue_digest carries the same information); no such mutant was run.
- Conclusion: DECOMPOSED-ONLY. This agrees with the original UNREACHABLE-ISOLATED record for this member and does not change it.

## 4. GRAFT construction and why the candidate state is otherwise valid
Construction: world d1 and world d2 are both genuine (production code minted both decisions through GovernedAgeWorkflow.decide). The d1 decision's persisted effective_configuration member (version, digest, members) is copied verbatim over the d2 decision's member in the store file (run.json); nothing is edited or resealed; the grafted digest recomputes. World d2 is then restarted over that store and `execute(P2, D2)` is called. Label: unsigned-store write; the store has no integrity protection against its writer (documented limit); no guard is disabled.
Validity evidence (all PASS): grafted member == donor member byte-for-byte; store diff versus the pristine d2 copy is confined to the member path; the production constructor and store reader accept the store and reload the decision; classifier returns "mismatch" (not "invalid"/malformed); the complementary diff against the genuine live-d2 decision for the same proposal has an EMPTY base diff; an untouched copy of the d2 store executes in the same world (acknowledged, 1 call); a neutral graft of an identical-domain member executes (the write path itself does not cause refusal). Thus the only difference between the executing and the refused d2 states is the member's authority_domain leaf and its digest.
What this does not show: that an attacker or operator would have such a write, nor any natural route; it shows the comparison and live derivation are member-sensitive on the real execute path.

## 6. Adverse findings
None against the implementation in the cases run. Observations, not defects: (1) the refusal code authorization_binding_changed is emitted for any binding difference (bounded.py:1692-1693), so attribution requires the complementary diff; (2) an acknowledged execute appends two attempt records (attempted, acknowledged) under one attempt id; (3) pydantic emits deprecation warnings (instance access to model_fields) from the harness's resolver-retarget helper, harmless; (4) PytestDeprecationWarning from pytest-asyncio configuration in the environment.
